title: Enterprise Onboarding + Integration + Escalation + QBR Playbook
author: Asha Patel
summary: Comprehensive playbook covering enterprise onboarding milestones, pre-launch integration checklist, standard escalation paths, known issues and workarounds, and QBR/health-check templates for Customer Success engagement.
onboarding_overview: Purpose: Provide a repeatable, measurable onboarding and go-live runbook for enterprise customers using Redwood Inference Hosted, Dedicated, or Private deployments. Scope: Integration, security review, performance verification, operational handoff, and first 90-day success plan. Goals: 1) Achieve successful production traffic within agreed launch window; 2) Meet latency and availability targets; 3) Establish ongoing support and QBR cadence. Key stakeholders: Customer Success (CS), Solutions Engineering (SE), Product, Infra/Eng, Security, Customer IT. Typical timeline: Discovery (weeks -4 to -3), Integration (weeks -3 to -1), Pre-launch verification (week 0), Launch + hypercare (weeks 0 to +2), QBR & maturity planning (30/60/90 days).
integration_checklist:
Pre-requisites (complete before integration):
- Signed contract and assigned Customer Success owner
- Customer network access & allowlist (if Private/VPC)
- API keys & audit user created
- Model versions pinned for initial rollout
- Service account and KMS details (if using customer KMS)

Mandatory integration steps:
1) Access & Identity
   - Verify SSO/OAuth or API key configuration.
   - Confirm RBAC roles: dev, ops, read-only analytics.
2) Networking
   - For Private deployments: verify VPC peering, route tables, and NAT/GW.
   - Confirm IP allowlist for Hosted endpoints.
3) Security & Compliance
   - Exchange security questionnaire and complete penetration test schedule if required.
   - Validate data residency and retention settings.
4) Model & Performance
   - Confirm model variant and quantization profile.
   - Run baseline perf tests with representative prompts: collect p50/p95 latency and tokens/sec.
5) Observability & Alerts
   - Hook up tracing (OpenTelemetry) endpoint and assign log retention.
   - Configure alerting thresholds (see "ownership_and_service_level_expectations" below).
6) Data and Prompting
   - Provision prompt templates and example evaluations.
   - Run 50-200 sample inference calls through customer integration to validate outputs.

Deliverables before go-live: integration sign-off document (SE + CS), baseline perf report, security sign-off, and runbook for hypercare.
escalation_playbook:
Purpose: Provide a clear, time-boxed escalation path for incidents and customer-reported issues during onboarding and production.

Severity definitions and SLOs:
- Sev-1 (Critical): production outage or >50% customers affected, system unavailable, major data loss. Target initial response: 15 minutes. Target SLA update cadence: every 30 minutes.
- Sev-2 (High): degraded service impacting significant functionality (e.g., p95 latency doubled). Initial response: 30 minutes.
- Sev-3 (Medium): feature impacts, intermittent errors, or minor performance regressions. Initial response: 4 hours.
- Sev-4 (Low): non-urgent requests, feature requests, or documentation issues. Initial response: 2 business days.

Escalation matrix (contact sequence):
1) Tier 1 Support (CS) — initial triage. Contact channels: support@redwoodinference.com, support Slack channel #support; phone escalation for enterprise: +1-415-555-0123. Owner: Customer Success.
2) Solutions Engineering — replicas, integration debug, feature flags. Pager: se-oncall@redwood.com. Owner: Solutions Engineering.
3) Eng Platform / Serving Runtime — performance, kernel issues, capacity. Pager: runtime-oncall@redwood.com. Owner: Eng Serving Runtime.
4) Infra / SRE — cloud/networking incidents and capacity limits. Pager: infra-oncall@redwood.com. Owner: Eng SRE.
5) Engineering Leadership & Executive Escalation — invoked for SEV-1 lasting >2 hours or customer executive request. Contacts listed in the internal escalation roster.

Escalation steps (ordered):
1) Triage & classification by CS.
2) Reproduce and collect diagnostics: request logs, request/response samples, timestamps, request IDs.
3) Open incident with incident ID using our incident template and notify owners.
4) If unresolved within response SLA, escalate to next owner immediately.
5) Provide regular SLA updates to customer (see Communications section).

Communications:
- Template update cadence: SEV-1: every 30 minutes; SEV-2: hourly until resolved; SEV-3/4: daily or per outcome.
- Update channels: customer Slack channel (preferred), email thread with CS lead, and support portal ticket.
- Post-incident: produce postmortem within 5 business days for SEV-1/2 and include root cause, impact, mitigations, and action items.
known_issues_and_workarounds:
This section lists recurring issues observed during enterprise onboarding and recommended temporary workarounds. Keep this page synced with 'known-issues-and-workarounds' parent page.

1) High p95 latency for long-sequence prompts
- Symptom: Customers observe p95 latency spikes on requests >2k tokens.
- Root cause: Batch sizing and KV cache miss leading to scheduling inefficiency.
- Workarounds: reduce batch_max_tokens, enable prefix/KV caching for repeated contexts, or pin a higher-throughput model variant (e.g., m-13b-amp -> m-13b-amp-quant).

2) Authorization failures after key rotation
- Symptom: 403s for previously working API keys.
- Root cause: delayed propagation in SSO/KMS sync for private deployments.
- Workarounds: verify service account mapping, retry after 5-10 minutes, use temporary admin API key issued by SE for emergency access.

3) Unexpected tokenization differences across model variants
- Symptom: truncated responses or off-by-one token counts when switching model variants.
- Root cause: tokenizer mismatch between model family versions.
- Workarounds: normalize tokenizer to canonical model tokenizer in client code; pin tokenizer version in integration checklist.

4) Embedding mismatch for similarity searches
- Symptom: drift in similarity ranking after model update.
- Root cause: embedding vector space shift.
- Workarounds: run a reindexing job for stored vectors, and run A/B evaluation using our eval harness before model rollouts.
support_process_and_routing:
Support channels and expected response SLAs:
- Support Portal: primary ticketing system for all customers. Tickets create event in CS tracker.
- Enterprise Slack: real-time operations/incident comms.
- Phone escalation: for agreed enterprise customers during business hours.

Routing rules:
- All SEV-1/2 incidents: immediate page to runtime-oncall and infra-oncall; CS to own customer communication.
- Integration/feature questions: route to Solutions Engineering; create a joint troubleshooting session within 48 hours.
- Billing/contract issues: route to Finance & Account Executive.

Runbook snippet (triage checklist):
1) Confirm customer identity and scope of impact.
2) Capture request IDs and timestamps.
3) Check service health dashboard and alerts for correlated signals.
4) Collect logs: request logs, worker logs, and controller logs.
5) If no immediate resolution, escalate per "escalation_playbook" matrix.

Ownership:
- Tier 1 (CS) owns communication and incident creation.
- SE owns integrations and reproduction.
- Eng owns fixes and rollouts.

Documentation: Link incidents to JIRA ticket for engineering tracking and to the CS onboarding record for customer history.
health_checks_and_qbr_templates:
Purpose: Provide a consistent hygiene & health assessment and QBR template for enterprise accounts to align on usage, performance, and roadmap.

30/60/90 health check template (to be completed by CS + SE):
- Executive Summary: adoption status, risks, and recommended actions.
- Usage Metrics: tokens/day, calls/sec, successful responses %, error rate % (7/30d).
- Performance Metrics: p50/p95 latency, average tokens per request, model variants in use.
- Cost & Efficiency: cost per 1k tokens, batching and cache hit rate recommendations.
- Security & Compliance: outstanding controls, open action items, audit logs configured.
- Roadmap & Next Steps: features to enable, performance tuning, model rollouts.

QBR agenda (1 hour recommended):
1) Introductions & goals (5m)
2) Adoption & metrics review (15m)
3) Performance & reliability review (15m)
4) Risk & action items (10m)
5) Roadmap & product asks (10m)
6) Wrap-up & next steps (5m)

Deliverables: QBR slide deck, action item tracker, follow-up ticket list. Store QBR artifacts in customer record and attach to related_pages.

Example QBR KPIs to surface: active endpoints, average latency (p50/p95), error rate, top prompt templates by volume, model drift alerts triggered, cost per request trends.
ownership_and_service_level_expectations:
SLOs for enterprise onboarding and early production:
- On-call response times: see "escalation_playbook" severity table.
- Availability target: 99.9% for Dedicated/Hosted during business hours for enterprise contracts.
- Latency targets: p50 < 120ms for small prompts, p95 < 700ms (varies by model family).
- Error budget & throttling: automatic throttling when error rate >2% for >15 minutes; customers notified via CS.

Roles & responsibilities:
- Customer Success: onboarding plan, weekly check-ins, communications, QBRs.
- Solutions Engineering: integration, baseline perf tests, runbook authoring.
- Eng Serving Runtime: performance investigations, kernel & scheduling fixes.
- Eng SRE: incident response, capacity planning, alerts.
